Walkthrough
A new --fetch (-f) command-line option was added to all ccusage commands, allowing users to specify a custom source (HTTPS URL or local file path) for model pricing data. This option is now integrated into the data loading and cost calculation logic, and the documentation has been updated to explain its usage and limitations.
Changes



File(s)
Change Summary




README.md
Documented new --fetch option, usage details, and updated examples.


src/shared-args.internal.ts
Added new fetch argument to shared CLI options.


src/commands/daily.tssrc/commands/monthly.tssrc/commands/session.ts
Passed fetch option from CLI context into data loading and mismatch detection functions.


src/data-loader.ts
Extended LoadOptions type with optional fetch property; passed to PricingFetcher.


src/pricing-fetcher.ts
Modified PricingFetcher to accept a source for pricing data (URL or file); updated logic.


src/debug.ts
Updated detectMismatches to accept and use fetch parameter.


src/fetch-cli.test.ts
Added tests for --fetch option covering caching, local and remote pricing sources, and error handling.



Sequence Diagram(s)

  
    
      sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant CLI
    participant DataLoader
    participant PricingFetcher

    User->>CLI: Run ccusage command with --fetch <source>
    CLI->>DataLoader: load*UsageData({ fetch: <source>, ... })
    DataLoader->>PricingFetcher: new PricingFetcher(<source>)
    PricingFetcher->>PricingFetcher: ensurePricingLoaded()
    alt Source is HTTPS URL
        PricingFetcher->>PricingFetcher: Fetch pricing from URL
    else Source is local file
        PricingFetcher->>PricingFetcher: Read pricing from file
    end
    PricingFetcher-->>DataLoader: Return pricing data
    DataLoader-->>CLI: Continue cost calculation

    
  
  
    
  
    
    
    Loading

Hi, I've tried adding the --offline parameter, but it doesn't work as expected. If my usage is incorrect, please let me know. I tested with my modified code (bunx ccusage-test) and it can successfully get the local proxy and use the proxy to access LiteLLM.

Problem: Node.js fetch() doesn't automatically read system proxy settings. Even when users set http_proxy/https_proxy environment variables, ccusage still attempts direct connections to the LiteLLM API, causing failures in corporate networks or proxy-required environments. This is particularly common in network-restricted regions like China.
My PR solution: Before making network requests, detect common proxy environment variables (http_proxy, https_proxy, etc.). If proxy configuration is detected, use undici's ProxyAgent to handle proxy connections, allowing fetch to access external services through the proxy. If no proxy is configured, maintain the original direct connection behavior, ensuring full backward compatibility.
The core issue is Node.js fetch()'s limitation - it doesn't automatically respect system proxy settings like other network tools (curl, browsers, etc.) do. My PR essentially fills this gap by adding the proxy support that fetch() should have had by default.

commit: 296ed08

Walkthrough
The changes enhance terminal output management by improving how content is cleared and written in the TerminalManager class. New methods were added for precise control over clearing previously written lines, and line tracking was introduced. In the live monitoring command, screen clearing responsibilities were refactored and short delays were added after clearing to ensure proper terminal updates.
Changes



File(s)
Change Summary




src/_terminal-utils.ts
Enhanced TerminalManager with line tracking, improved screen clearing using readline, added clearPreviousContent, clearLine, moveUp, moveToLineStart, and writeRaw methods, and updated write to track line counts.


src/commands/_blocks.live.ts
Added short delays after screen clearing, removed redundant clear from renderLiveDisplay, and centralized clearing logic in startLiveMonitoring.

    participant TerminalManager
    participant startLiveMonitoring
    participant renderLiveDisplay

    startLiveMonitoring->>TerminalManager: clearScreen()
    startLiveMonitoring->>startLiveMonitoring: await small delay
    alt No active session block

    else Active block found
        startLiveMonitoring->>TerminalManager: clearScreen()
        startLiveMonitoring->>startLiveMonitoring: await small delay
        startLiveMonitoring->>renderLiveDisplay: Render block
        renderLiveDisplay->>TerminalManager: write(block content)
    end

Walkthrough
This change adds tracking and display of Claude API usage limit reset times. It introduces a mechanism to extract reset timestamps from API error messages, propagates this information through internal data structures, and updates the live monitor and rendering logic to show a warning with the reset time when the usage limit is reached.
Changes



File(s)
Summary of Changes




src/data-loader.ts
Added optional content and isApiErrorMessage fields to schema; introduced getUsageLimitResetTime function; updated JSON parsing to use try-catch; loadSessionBlockData now includes usageLimitResetTime in entries.


src/_live-monitor.ts
Calls getUsageLimitResetTime and attaches usageLimitResetTime to usage entries in getActiveBlock.


src/_session-blocks.ts
Extended LoadedUsageEntry and SessionBlock types with optional usageLimitResetTime; aggregates this value in createBlock.


src/commands/blocks.ts
Includes usageLimitResetTime in JSON output for blocks in the blocksCommand.


src/_live-rendering.ts
Displays a red warning message with the usage limit reset time in the live display if applicable.

      sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant LiveMonitor
    participant DataLoader
    participant Renderer

    User->>LiveMonitor: Request live monitoring
    LiveMonitor->>DataLoader: Load session block data
    DataLoader->>DataLoader: Parse usage data, extract usageLimitResetTime
    DataLoader-->>LiveMonitor: Return entries with usageLimitResetTime
    LiveMonitor->>Renderer: Provide block data (with usageLimitResetTime)
    Renderer->>User: Display live usage, show reset warning if limit reached

Walkthrough
This update comprehensively refactors error handling throughout the codebase to use the Result utility from @praha/byethrow in place of traditional try-catch blocks. It updates multiple modules, adds relevant dependencies and configuration, and documents new error handling conventions in the code style guide.
Changes



File(s)
Change Summary




.mcp.json, package.json
Added @praha/byethrow and @praha/byethrow-mcp as dev dependencies; configured MCP server for byethrow-mcp.


CLAUDE.md
Documented new error handling conventions, recommending the use of Result over try-catch for functional style.


src/_live-monitor.ts, src/data-loader.ts,src/debug.ts, src/commands/_blocks.live.ts,src/pricing-fetcher.ts
Refactored all error handling for file reading, JSON parsing, and async operations to use Result.try and related utilities, replacing try-catch and catch handlers. Improved logging and statistics initialization in some modules.



Sequence Diagram(s)

  
    
      sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller
    participant FileSystem/Network
    participant Result
    Note over Caller,Result: Example: JSON parsing with Result.try

    Caller->>Result: Result.try(() => JSON.parse(line))
    alt Success
        Result-->>Caller: Success(parsedObject)
        Caller->>Caller: Continue processing
    else Failure
        Result-->>Caller: Failure(error)
        Caller->>Caller: Skip line or log error
    end

    
  
  
    
  
    
    
    Loading

  



  
    
      sequenceDiagram
    participant LiveMonitor
    participant FileSystem
    participant Result
    Note over LiveMonitor,Result: Reading and parsing files

    loop For each file
        LiveMonitor->>Result: Result.try(async () => readFile(file))
        alt File read succeeds
            Result-->>LiveMonitor: Success(fileContent)
            LiveMonitor->>Result: Result.try(() => JSON.parse(line))
            alt Parse succeeds
                Result-->>LiveMonitor: Success(parsedLine)
                LiveMonitor->>LiveMonitor: Validate and accumulate
            else Parse fails
                Result-->>LiveMonitor: Failure(error)
                LiveMonitor->>LiveMonitor: Skip line
            end
        else File read fails
            Result-->>LiveMonitor: Failure(error)
            LiveMonitor->>LiveMonitor: Skip file
        end
    end

    
  
  
    
  
    
    
    Loading

ryoppippi/ccusage#168: Refactors startLiveMonitoring (same function as in this PR) to add cache clearing, affecting the same code region with a different focus.

Poem

In the warren where errors once hopped,
Now Result bounces, exceptions all stopped.
No more try-catch, just hop and check—
If failure is found, we scurry, not wreck.
Byethrow’s the burrow, our code’s cozy den,
Rabbits rejoice: clean error handling again! 🐇✨

Thank you very much for your contribution and the time you spent working on this!
That said, we’re currently prioritising JSON output as the main format, as it’s more versatile and widely used in modern tooling. Maintaining support for both CSV and JSON would increase the complexity of the codebase and maintenance cost, so we’ve decided to stick with JSON only for now.
If you’d like to use CSV, you can easily convert the JSON output using jq. For example:
bunx ccusage --json | jq -r '.daily | .[] | [.date, .totalCost] | @csv'
We really appreciate your interest in improving ccusage, and hope you’ll continue contributing in the future! 🙏

## Walkthrough

The changes update the `PricingFetcher` class and related code to adopt a monadic error-handling style using `Result` utilities from `@praha/byethrow`. Methods now return `ResultAsync` types, replacing explicit async/await and try-catch blocks with composable pipelines. Calls to `calculateCostFromTokens` unwrap `Result` values. Dependency versions for `@praha/byethrow` packages are also upgraded.

| package.json                    | Updated "@praha/byethrow" dev dependency from "^0.3.0" to "^0.4.1" and "@praha/byethrow-mcp" from "^0.0.7" to "^0.0.10".             |
| src/data-loader.ts, src/debug.ts | Wrapped calls to `fetcher.calculateCostFromTokens` with `Result.unwrap` to extract values from `Result` types.                    |
| src/pricing-fetcher.ts          | Refactored `PricingFetcher` methods to use `Result.ResultAsync` for composable error handling; updated method signatures and logic. |

This update introduces weekly aggregation and reporting features to the codebase. New types, schemas, and helper functions for weekly buckets are added. The cost calculation, CLI command registry, and tests are updated accordingly. Minor dependency version changes and test environment updates are also included.

Weekly Types and Utilitiessrc/_types.ts
Added weeklyDateSchema, WeeklyDate, Bucket, createWeeklyDate, and createBucket for weekly date validation and bucket type support.


Generic and Weekly Data Aggregationsrc/data-loader.ts
Introduced weekly aggregation logic: new schemas/types (weeklyUsageSchema, WeeklyUsage, bucketUsageSchema, BucketUsage), helper getDateWeek, generic loadBucketUsageData, and loadWeeklyUsageData. Refactored monthly aggregation to use the new generic function. Added comprehensive tests for weekly aggregation.


Cost Calculation Updatesrc/calculate-cost.ts
Updated calculateTotals to support the new WeeklyUsage data type in its input, allowing aggregation over weekly data.


CLI Command Registrysrc/commands/index.ts
Registered a new "weekly" CLI subcommand by importing and mapping weeklyCommand in the subCommands map.


Weekly CLI Commandsrc/commands/weekly.ts
Added new exported weeklyCommand for generating weekly usage reports, supporting JSON/table output, filtering, ordering, breakdowns, and debug reporting. Implements aggregation, formatting, and output logic for weekly data.


Weekday Constantssrc/_consts.ts
Added WEEK_DAYS constant as a tuple of weekday strings from "sunday" to "saturday" for use in weekly aggregation logic.

Status line caching and APIsrc/commands/statusline.ts
Added disk-backed per-session semaphore (Limo JSON) with fields for lastOutput, transcriptMtime, isUpdating, pid, etc.; cache validation now uses transcript file mtime and configurable refresh interval; coordinates concurrent updates via pid/isUpdating; persists semaphore on success and resets flags on failure; introduced helpers for file mtime and semaphore management; public API extended with cache (boolean, default true) and refreshInterval (number, default DEFAULT_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS).

  CLI->>Sem: read semaphore for sessionId
  Sem-->>CLI: semaphore (maybe lastOutput, isUpdating, transcriptMtime)
  CLI->>FS: stat transcript (currentMtime)
  alt cache disabled
    CLI->>Proc: compute status line
    Proc-->>CLI: result
    CLI-->>User: output
  else cache enabled

      CLI->>Proc: compute status line
      Proc-->>CLI: result
      alt success
        CLI->>Sem: persist {lastOutput, lastUpdateTime, transcriptMtime, isUpdating=false, pid=null}
        CLI-->>User: output
      else failure
        CLI->>Sem: reset isUpdating=false, pid=null (if enabled)
        CLI-->>User: emit cached lastOutput or error
      end
    end

A bit of analysis from gpt-5-codex:

In the raw Codex logs, total_tokens = input_tokens + output_tokens even when reasoning_output_tokens is non‑zero. Example (2025‑09‑14T06:48:05Z):
input=12 460, output=1 042, reasoning=1 024, total=13 502.
The delta output - reasoning = 18 lines up with the short assistant reply that was actually shown in the terminal. The extra 1 024 tokens are the hidden chain‑of‑thought that the
model emitted, and they’re already counted inside output_tokens.

That pattern holds across the entire dataset. I scanned /home/code/.codex/sessions and found 2 015 reasoning events; in every single case output_tokens ≥ reasoning_output_tokens, and
total_tokens stayed at input + output—never input + output + reasoning. So the recorder is already folding the reasoning stream into the output_tokens figure.
Because of that, the current cost helper (calculateCostUSD) is double counting: it feeds outputTokens + reasoningOutputTokens into the pricing calculation even though those reasoning
tokens were already included in outputTokens. The right thing to do is bill on outputTokens alone (if you still want a separate “reasoning” column in reports, display it for insight but
don’t add it again for billing).

the reporting logic should subtract reasoning if you want the “Output” column to show only user‑visible tokens).
